{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABZgRIFQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhDHZ3M", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 55, "title": "Implement non-interlaced rectangular OBJ sizes and square-half vertical flipping", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `de7796f9d82c01b321f906a7b974df76eb23d4fc`, `Ppu::objects` uses one scalar dimension for visibility, horizontal iteration and both flips. OBSEL selectors 6 and 7 both select 16×16/32×32, truncating rectangular objects. See [the renderer](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/de7796f9d82c01b321f906a7b974df76eb23d4fc/crates/snes-core/src/ppu.rs#L578).

This is the next bounded implementation identified by the supplied latest assessment. No regression was identified within Issue #53's supported domain, and the supplied open-Issue list is empty. Rectangular OBJ rendering is not covered by the completed improvements.

## Expected outcome

Implement independent OBJ width and height for static, non-interlaced rendering, including the documented rectangular vertical-flip rule.

The complete OBSEL `$2101[7:5]` table is:

| Selector | OAM size bit clear | OAM size bit set |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | 8×8 | 16×16 |
| 1 | 8×8 | 32×32 |
| 2 | 8×8 | 64×64 |
| 3 | 16×16 | 32×32 |
| 4 | 16×16 | 64×64 |
| 5 | 32×32 | 64×64 |
| 6 | 16×32 | 32×64 |
| 7 | 16×32 | 32×32 |

Fullsnes labels selectors 6–7 reserved in its introductory field description but explicitly lists their undocumented dimensions. They must not be rejected or treated as square aliases. Its OAM description identifies the per-object size bit. [Fullsnes: SNES PPU Sprites](https://problemkaputt.de/fullsnes.htm#snesppuspritesobjs)

For local destination coordinates `(col,row)` and selected dimensions `(W,H)`:

- Determine vertical inclusion using the eight-bit wrapped Y displacement and `H`; iterate horizontal pixels using `W`.
- Horizontal flip maps `col` to `W−1−col`.
- Vertical flip preserves the ordering of the two stacked square halves of a rectangular object and reverses rows within each half. Derived equation: `source_row = row XOR (W−1)`. For 16×32, tile-row order `0,1,2,3` becomes `1,0,3,2`; for 32×64, `0…7` becomes `3,2,1,0,7,6,5,4`. Square objects retain ordinary full-height flipping. These equations implement Anomie's explicit rectangular exception. [Anomie's Register Doc, revision 1157: OBSEL and SPRITES](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gilligan/snesdev/master/docs/snes_registers.txt)

Retain OBJ character-table addressing: horizontal tile increments wrap within the low nibble; vertical increments wrap within the high nibble, without crossing into the OAM name-table bit. Preserve OBSEL base/name selection and 64-KiB VRAM byte wrapping. [Fullsnes: Video Memory, “16x16 (and bigger) Tiles”](https://problemkaputt.de/fullsnes.htm#snesppuvideomemoryvram)

Scope is OBJ dimensions and their direct effects on visibility, flips and character selection. Preserve existing palettes, transparency, priorities, routing and OAM access behavior. Overflow flags, exact evaluation/fetch limits, priority-rotation oddities, X=−256 special handling, OBJ interlace, hires-specific accuracy and raster timing remain outside this Issue.

## Context and reproduction

Existing [OAM tests](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/de7796f9d82c01b321f906a7b974df76eb23d4fc/crates/snes-core/src/ppu_oam_tests.rs) exercise ports and rotation. The [pseudo-hires routing test](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/de7796f9d82c01b321f906a7b974df76eb23d4fc/crates/snes-core/tests/ppu_pseudo_hires.rs#L195) uses an ordinary small square OBJ. Neither establishes rectangular sizing or flipping.

Minimal counterexample:

1. Initialize an original asymmetric 16×32 character image, OBJ palette and OAM under forced blank. Keep unrelated objects off the sampled rows and stay below existing sprite/tile limits.
2. Set OBSEL selector 6 or 7 and clear that object's size bit.
3. Enable OBJ on the main screen, disable color math/interlace and render through the bottom boundary.
4. Expect visible pixels at local rows 16–31 and backdrop at row 32. Baseline truncates at row 16.

A second counterexample uses selector 6 with the size bit set: rows 32–63 should exist. A flip counterexample must distinguish square-half reversal from full-height reversal.

The repository's [Issue #43 specification record](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/de7796f9d82c01b321f906a7b974df76eb23d4fc/docs/issue-43-validation.md#specification-record-written-before-production-changes) identifies the references and recorded versions. Its OAM-port approximations do not establish rendering geometry. This planning pass inspected source and tests; no suites were rerun.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Implement the table and independent dimensions in `Ppu::objects`, including square-half vertical flipping. Avoid unrelated renderer or scheduler refactoring.
- [ ] Add original MIT tests in `crates/snes-core/tests/ppu_obj_sizes.rs`. Exercise all eight selectors and both OAM size-bit values. For rectangular cases, check all four flip combinations, asymmetric pixels within tiles, tile boundaries, square-half boundaries, final included rows/columns and adjacent backdrop pixels. Include square-size controls with flips.
- [ ] Add independent pixel vectors for partially left/right-clipped objects, Y wrap across 255→0, character-column and character-row wrapping, both name tables, and a wrapping OBSEL base/name address. Keep geometry fixtures below evaluation limits. Expected pixels must use literal vectors or independently constructed image crops, never production addressing/rendering helpers.
- [ ] Add a bounded original CPU-executed cartridge fixture covering selector 6 small/large, selector 7 small/large and rectangular vertical flip. CPU instructions initialize registers, VRAM, CGRAM and both OAM tables under forced blank. The host supplies only the cartridge/input, advances execution and observes completion markers and pixels; it must not patch PPU state.
- [ ] Use that source-built fixture in an automated browser check of actual Wasm framebuffer and canvas pixels, including lower rectangular halves and a flip boundary. Add its exact reproducible command to the validation record. Record source, license, generated hashes and execution bounds in `tests/roms/PROVENANCE.md`; acquire no commercial ROM or firmware.
- [ ] Demonstrate new rectangular-height tests fail against the exact baseline and pass with the implementation. Record failures separately from unchanged square controls; do not substitute a baseline compilation failure for a behavioral counterexample.
- [ ] Pass the following Rust checks, using the repository CI toolchain (Rust 1.99.0) and verifying the selected Clippy version:

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --locked
cargo test --locked -p snes-core --test ppu_obj_sizes
cargo test --locked -p snes-core --lib oam
cargo test --locked -p snes-core --test ppu_oam_access --test ppu_oam_reload --test ppu_hires --test ppu_pseudo_hires --test direct_color
```

- [ ] Pass existing source-built CPU, SPC700 and HDMA gates and browser regressions from [README validation](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/de7796f9d82c01b321f906a7b974df76eb23d4fc/README.md#validate):

```sh
python3 tools/build-test-tools.py --spc
python3 tools/hardware-tests.py --ca65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ca65" --ld65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ld65" --spcasm "$PWD/.cache/tools/spcasm/target/release/spcasm"
python3 tools/ppu-test.py --bass "$PWD/.cache/tools/bass-untech/bass/out/bass-untech"
python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
npm --prefix web ci
npm --prefix web run build
(cd web && npx playwright install chromium)
SNES_TEST_PORT=18085 npm --prefix web test -- --grep-invert '301 seconds'
```

Preserve existing Castle/Memory sources, pins, output hashes, replay inputs, durations, gameplay/audio assertions and negative controls. Do not weaken assertions to accommodate this change.

- [ ] Update README and a validation record with cited specification sections, coordinate derivations, commands, actual outcomes and remaining uncertainty. Preserve all 24 inventory categories and their full scopes from the [existing inventory](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/de7796f9d82c01b321f906a7b974df76eb23d4fc/docs/issue-53-validation.md#remaining-uncertainty-and-inventory). `ppu-objects` remains partial; no category becomes verified through these bounded tests. Explicitly retain overflow/evaluation, rotation, interlace, hires interactions and fetch timing as remaining work. Passing these gates establishes neither complete hardware accuracy nor commercial compatibility.

## Optional validation

Additional original scenes combining rectangular objects with BG priority and layer windows, below evaluation limits.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
